video_title: History Rising: A Conversation with Head Natalie Nakase Ahead of the WNBA Finals

quotes.speaker: Natalie Nakase
quotes.summary_phrase: Natalie Nakase on her approach to building a competitive roster
quotes.excerpt: I hand pick players that are very competitive. However I could motivate, support, encourage my players
quotes.quote: Because I got to pick from the expansion draft, I hand pick players that are very competitive. However I could motivate, support, encourage my players to be consistent, I think that's going to be key.

quotes.speaker: Natalie Nakase
quotes.summary_phrase: Natalie Nakase on using film study to develop coaching strategies
quotes.excerpt: It's therapy for me to be honest. I could watch film for days because now from a
quotes.quote: It's therapy for me to be honest. I could watch film for days because now from a coach's perspective, I like to see their moves, their counters. So that's kind of what I study. Like, okay, if we're killing them with this set, how are they going to counter it? So that's what I like to do. I like to watch a full game as well, because when teams are struggling or players are struggling, like cool, great, I might throw that out there. You know what I mean? And then obviously, watching anything from high school to college, you can see any type of random tactic. I love to mix in box-and-one, triangle-and-two, like out of a timeout just fuck it up. Like just mess it up. I like the surprise type of defense.

quotes.speaker: Natalie Nakase
quotes.summary_phrase: Natalie Nakase on the influence of Tyronn Lue on her coaching
quotes.excerpt: I'm very lucky to have a mentor, a friend, who sees the game to me the best
quotes.quote: What I've learned from Tyronn Lue, I mean, he's a phone call away, so I'm very lucky to have a mentor, a friend, who sees the game to me the best in the world. And so to have his knowledge, like literally, like playoffs, I'm giving him a call, what did you see? And I know he's watching. So just to kind of have that, but Ty is all about like preparation. You have to study, now you got to study your opponent, that's why like the film comes in, and you have to just be ready to counter.

quotes.speaker: Natalie Nakase
quotes.summary_phrase: Natalie Nakase on the core values of her coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: Competitive, like across the board, from I mean my rebounders to my scout guys, our front office
quotes.quote: Competitive, like across the board, from I mean my rebounders to my scout guys, our front office is competitive, like super competitive. Secondly, connected, like we have to be connected, both offensively and defensively. Like the more we communicate, the better we're going to be connected. And then the last one I've kind of been going back and forth, but again, watching tons of NBA, like you got to play consistently, and I think that's hard.

quotes.speaker: Chris Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Johnson on the importance of professionalism and preparation for players
quotes.excerpt: My message to them is about professionalism and loving the craft. You have to focus on winning
quotes.quote: My message to them is about professionalism and loving the craft. You have to focus on winning the day. So instead of looking at what you can't do, play the hand that you have. You could be traded, somebody can be injured, and if you're not prepared, it's going to show, and you lose the opportunity. So the flip coin of that is playing ones every day, playing twos every day, because the people that play heavy minutes are not going to be hooping every day in a physical practice. They're going to be able to get treatment and get everything that they need to be ready for the competition of the next game. But the guys that don't play and the women that don't play, they have to be in love with the game of basketball.

quotes.speaker: Chris Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Johnson on the dangers of complacency for NBA players
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes complacency and pointing the finger will have you out of the league. So you need people
quotes.quote: Sometimes complacency and pointing the finger will have you out of the league. So you need people talking directly to you and saying, hey, it's on you. Win your day, daily routine, prepare, take care of your body, and you're always interviewing for your next job. The players that do that, they win eventually. They go from being a bench player to rotational player to being a starter, and some going to be All-Stars. So there's no window that you can put them in or box, if you love the game.

quotes.speaker: D Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: D Wright on the importance of veteran guidance and hard work
quotes.excerpt: I give a lot of credit to where I went in my career, not only having good vets
quotes.quote: I give a lot of credit to where I went in my career, not only having good vets, but Keith Atkins. He was one of the best for my journey and my development because he made sure I was working on every single thing every single day. I came in as a athletic slasher and I ended my career being known as a shooter. And that was all because of the development and the time and the hours that I spent in that gym.

quotes.speaker: Natalie Nakase
quotes.summary_phrase: Natalie Nakase on the importance of clear communication with players
quotes.excerpt: But it's more too like your delivery to the player, right? Like how you deliver it and get
quotes.quote: But it's more too like your delivery to the player, right? Like how you deliver it and get them to listen and like instantly and believe it. Because a lot of times, you know, as you guys have trainers and you guys are so elite, and Chelsea Gray is the elite, the point guard, where sometimes as you tell her stuff, you're like, shit, is this true? But she just, again, light away. Yeah, because your delivery is so good.

quotes.speaker: Chris Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Johnson on the importance of understanding a player's perspective
quotes.excerpt: I try to take a step back and I try to get in the player's perspective. So you
quotes.quote: I try to take a step back and I try to get in the player's perspective. So you can have a wealth of knowledge, but the knowledge may not apply to that individual. So I don't want to take a step back and I actually want to see how they see the game. So it's not just physical, it's about how they interpret and how they see it. And if I can understand how they see the game, then I can get them to understand other parts of the game that can advance them.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on Erik Spoelstra's ability to define player roles
quotes.excerpt: Spo was great at when it was playoff time, really defining roles. Like we signed contracts in the
quotes.quote: Spo was great at when it was playoff time, really defining roles. Like we signed contracts in the playoffs. Right? Everybody had to stand up and sign a contract in front of the team, but he would define your role, not you. Your your season has defined your role for you. And now he's he's went through and he's watched your entire season and he's going to tell you exactly who you are and what your role on this team needs to be.

quotes.speaker: Chris Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Johnson on the importance of player management and communication
quotes.excerpt: And when you mention someone like Ty Lue, Ty Lue is known for player relationship. Yes he is.
quotes.quote: And when you mention someone like Ty Lue, Ty Lue is known for player relationship. Yes he is. So it doesn't matter, I'm not worried about your scheme. I think you got an edge because I believe that you care. And those player management is important.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on the importance of having a calming leader
quotes.excerpt: I need someone in the moments of chaos that I can look to and they're as calm
quotes.quote: I need someone in the moments of chaos that I can look to and they're as calm or calmer than me. Enter Pat Riley into the this into this picture because Pat Riley was the calmest leader on the sideline when everything is going chaotic and you like, and he's like, so you need that. And the second one I need is I need a coach that I can curse at, that I can motherfuck, and he can motherfuck me back because this is really for the head coach. But I need you to be the sounding board for these and I but I need you to be able to give it back to me. And so I always say David Fizdale was mine during my championship runs in Miami because I couldn't say this to Spo. But I used to be pissed like, why is Udonis Haslem in the game? What the?

quotes.speaker: Chris Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Johnson on Phil Jackson's management of Dennis Rodman
quotes.excerpt: You see some of the best coaches like, you know Phil Jackson, when you watch how he handled
quotes.quote: You see some of the best coaches like, you know Phil Jackson, when you watch how he handled Dennis Rodman. Phil Jackson allowed Dennis Rodman to go to Vegas. That's real. That's real. That's genius. He's like he he let him go to Vegas. He needs this for week for us to win. That's a smart coach. This is what I'm saying. He's a Am I right or wrong? And they won. It's not an ego problem. So Phil being Zenful, like his ability to not make it about him, and not to create rules that he got to break. He was flexible and paying attention, and I think in our in the world of basketball, we become inflexible sometimes. It's a lot of red tape.
